html:
A railway tunnel under the Tsugaru Strait in Japan, joining the main island of Honshu to Hokkaido. It is about 54 km long, with some 23 km under the seabed, and opened in 1988.

The idea gained force after 1954, when the ferry Toya Maru sank in a typhoon in the strait and over a thousand people died. Work began in earnest in 1971 and took seventeen years through soft rock, faults and floods; dozens of workers were killed.

By the time it opened, air travel had taken much of the traffic. For decades it was the longest railway tunnel in the world, until the Gotthard Base Tunnel in Switzerland opened in 2016. The Channel Tunnel has a longer stretch under the sea. Since 2016 the Shinkansen bullet trains have run through it to Hokkaido, alongside freight trains. It is one of the great engineering works of postwar Japan.
